rules: National Polygon Service contains three licensed chargeable datasets: National Polygon, Title Descriptor, and Title Number and UPRN Look Up.
National Polygon data shows the indicative shape and position of registered-title boundaries in England and Wales.
Every freehold or leasehold registered title has at least one HMLR index polygon.
HMLR reports more than 25 million titles and about 28 million polygons in the National Polygon Service.
HMLR index polygons are mapped against Ordnance Survey MasterMap large-scale mapping.
National Polygon Service monthly delivery includes a full dataset, change-only updates, and validation files.
The Title Number and UPRN Look Up dataset does not have a change-only file.
National Polygon Service files are updated on the second working day of the month and contain data for the previous month.
A National Polygon complete file contains the current data including all changes that happened during the month.
A National Polygon change-only file contains data changed since the previous monthly release.
A National Polygon validation file is provided to check that downloaded data is complete/correct.
HMLR large-scale source mapping is captured at 1:1,250 in urban areas, 1:2,500 in semi-urban and rural areas, and 1:10,000 in mountain and moorland areas.
HMLR states that overlaps, gaps, slivers, and underlaps exist in National Polygon data and can be either genuine or inconsistent.
HMLR technical overlapping polygons can arise from mapping inconsistencies and do not necessarily describe a real conflict of registered titles.
HMLR actual overlaps can occur where two or more registered titles include the same land or property and are resolved upon application.
INSPIRE Index Polygons are a National Polygon subset with a simpler attribute set including identifier, creation date, and last-updated date.
Each registered estate or interest has a unique title number and a title number can have only one class of title.
A pending registration application can have a title number while estate interest and class-of-title information are still absent.
HMLR states that title tenure does not change, while a non-absolute class of title can be upgraded when sufficient evidence is supplied.
HMLR ingests an AddressBase change-only update every six weeks; published UPRN linkage data shows only the last change made within the maintenance cycle.
Planning Data provides more than 100 planning and housing datasets for England through one consistent API.
A coordinate query constructs a point from latitude and longitude and returns entities whose geometry intersects that point.
Multiple dataset parameters in one coordinate query return matches from any of the selected datasets.
Planning Data recommends UPRN queries through q as more precise than coordinates for registered properties.
Planning Data explicitly warns that no API result does not prove that no planning constraint exists because coverage varies by area.
Planning Data documents 337 local planning authorities in its all-LPA example.
The geometry_entity parameter can use the geometry of a known entity such as an LPA boundary for spatial filtering.
Listed-building entities can carry listed_building_grade directly, without a separate grade lookup.
The planning-application specification is still in development and local planning authorities are not currently required to share application data to it.
Raw geometry searches accept WKT coordinates in WGS84 EPSG:4326.
Planning Data recommends incrementing offset by the request limit when manually paginating large result sets.
Entity responses can expose pre-built next, previous, first, and last pagination links.
The portfolio-screening API has no batch endpoint and is documented as one request per property.
The field parameter is recommended to reduce portfolio-screening response payloads to required attributes.
Planning Data recommends polite rate limiting between per-property API requests.
For hundreds of properties or more, Planning Data recommends bulk downloads and local spatial intersection.
Planning Data describes bulk downloads as a stable snapshot for portfolio processing.
Bulk downloads can be CSV, JSON, GeoJSON where applicable, and Parquet; Parquet is described as well suited to large datasets.
Planning Data states that the API is still beta and may change for production-ready systems.
The dataset list endpoint is GET /dataset.{extension}, where extension is json or html; the OpenAPI file can be used to generate a client library.
The Survey Index OGC Features landing page identifies the service as a Defra Network WFS server provided by the Environment Agency.
The Survey Index OGC Features service exposes a machine-processable API document conformant to OpenAPI 3.
The Survey Index OGC Features service exposes a collection page listing available feature collections.
The Survey Index OGC Features service declares OGC API Features Core conformance.
The Survey Index OGC Features service declares OAS 3.0 conformance.
The Survey Index OGC Features service declares HTML representation conformance.
The Survey Index OGC Features service declares GeoJSON representation conformance.
The Survey Index OGC Features service declares CRS extension conformance.
The Survey Index OGC Features service declares Features Filter conformance.
The Survey Index OGC Features service declares Filter conformance.
The Survey Index OGC Features service declares Search conformance.
The Survey Index OGC Features service declares GeoServer ECQL conformance.
The Survey Index OGC Features service declares CQL2 basic conformance.
The Survey Index OGC Features service declares CQL2 advanced comparison-operator conformance.
The Survey Index OGC Features service declares CQL2 spatial-operator conformance.
The Survey Index OGC Features service declares sorting conformance through the OGC API Records sorting requirement.
The Survey Index OGC Features service declares feature-id query conformance.
The LIDAR_Composite_1m_DTM_2022_extents collection stores geometries in EPSG:27700 and publishes a geographic extent of approximately -7.116,49.84 to 2.118,55.886.
The 1m DTM extent collection exposes filename and tilename as string queryables, resolution as numeric, and survey start/end as DateTime queryables.
The 1m DTM extent collection publishes HTML, KML, GML 3.2, CSV, JSON, OGC Features JSON, and GeoJSON representations for collection data.
OS Terrain 50 XML metadata follows the GEMINI metadata standard used by Ordnance Survey for UK Location Programme and INSPIRE commitments.
OS Terrain 50 supplies GEMINI-style metadata on a per-tile basis as well as national product metadata.
Terrain 50 tile metadata records the product name OS Terrain 50.
Terrain 50 tile metadata records whether the spatial representation is grid DTM or vector contours.
Terrain 50 tile metadata uses the 10km National Grid tile reference as the tile title/reference.
Terrain 50 metadata classifies the topic category as the INSPIRE elevation theme.
The Terrain 50 processing date is the date the tile was created by Ordnance Survey, not the date of the real-world survey/change.
Terrain 50 metadata carries an incrementing version number indicating how many times the tile has been published.
Terrain 50 metadata records whether a change is a creation or a revision using change metadata and lineage.
Terrain 50 lineage can state that a tile was created from new imagery, partly revised from new imagery, or checked against new imagery with no change.
Ordnance Survey provides an XSLT viewing stylesheet to render Terrain metadata XML as easier-to-read HTML.
The Terrain ASCII auxiliary XML supplies min, max, mean, and standard-deviation height statistics intended to make colour ramps consistent across adjacent tiles.
Terrain 50 ASCII grid files declare 200 columns.
Terrain 50 ASCII grid files declare 200 rows.
Each Terrain 50 grid pixel is 50 metres by 50 metres.
Terrain 50 grid height values are presented to the nearest 0.1 metre.
Terrain 50 ASCII heights represent the height calculated at the centre of each pixel.
Terrain 50 grid rows progress west to east, with the next row starting 50 metres south of the previous row.
Terrain 50 GML feature identifiers use the form os.t50.<tile-name>.<sequential-number>, with geometry identifiers adding a .geom suffix.
Terrain 50 is updated by whole-tile refresh and Ordnance Survey states there are no plans for feature-based change-only updates.

Exact candidate WCS/coverage GeoTIFF bytes, SHA, NoData handling, and numeric heights remain absent.
Terrain50 productId and direct OpenData download route are strongly corroborated, but official product-details JSON readback remains absent.
Terrain50 TQ29 bytes/SHA and row149 col173/174 numeric values remain absent.
